title: Dispatch: Make serialized campaign position self-sorting (attempt 3)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.1 (attempt 3) — one focused change on top of attempts 1 and 2.

Attempts 1 (ce3f9a5) and 2 (88060a7) are ACCEPTED and stay. compareCampaignPositions is now correct: ordinal-first with codepoint tie-breaks, well covered by tests that provably fail against the old source. Do not revisit any of that. This attempt fixes one remaining defect the supervisor found in review.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.1.3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.1.3, cut from 88060a7 on eshyra-jhpt.1.2, so both prior attempts are already present. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 5 (correctness, forward hazard for eshyra-jhpt.2) — the SERIALIZED position is still session-first, so it is not self-sorting.
The comparator was fixed to lead with the ordinal, but formatCampaignPosition still emits `cp1~<session>~<turn>~<12-digit ordinal>`. Chronology is therefore recoverable only by parsing. Any consumer that sorts or range-compares the STRING — which is exactly what the projection hands to discovery as `effectivePosition: string`, and exactly what eshyra-jhpt.2 will store in a TEXT column — gets the wrong answer.

Reproduced, ordering:
    true chronological order        SQL `ORDER BY effective_position` yields
    cp1~s2~t1~000000000005          cp1~s10~t1~000000000006
    cp1~s10~t1~000000000006         cp1~s2~t1~000000000005
    cp1~s3~t1~000000000007          cp1~s3~t1~000000000007

Reproduced, and worse, the range predicate .2 needs for "active rules at position":
    rule   cp1~s2~t1~000000000005   (ordinal 5, chronologically active)
    cutoff cp1~s10~t1~000000000006  (ordinal 6, current position)
    ordinal 5 <= 6                          -> true  (rule IS active)
    'cp1~s2~...' <= 'cp1~s10~...'           -> false (rule is DROPPED)
An active campaign rule would be silently missing from the active set. eshyra-jhpt.2's acceptance criteria require deterministic active-at-position queries and eshyra-jhpt.4 requires DM/auditor set parity; a natural SQL implementation over this encoding violates both, and the bug would look like a storage defect rather than an encoding one.

FIX: make the canonical serialized form self-sorting by leading with the zero-padded ordinal, e.g. `cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~<encoded session>~<encoded turn>`, so that lexical/byte order over canonical strings equals chronological order and `ORDER BY` and `<=` are correct in SQL without parsing. Update formatCampaignPosition and parseCampaignPosition together, keep the round-trip and the canonical-form check, and keep the `cp1~` version prefix. compareCampaignPositions should keep comparing parsed fields (it is correct and explicit); the point of this change is that consumers who never parse are also correct.

Also update the module doc comment: it currently documents the old layout. State the new layout and add one line recording WHY the ordinal leads — that byte order over canonical positions must equal chronological order so downstream SQL ordering and range predicates are correct without parsing.

TESTS
- Update the existing format/parse assertions to the new layout.
- Add a test asserting the self-sorting property directly: build positions across sessions with lexically misleading ids (the s2/s10/s3 case above), map them to canonical strings, and assert that a plain string sort equals the chronological order, and that a `<=` string range predicate agrees with the ordinal comparison. This is the property that was missing; assert it on the strings, not only through compareCampaignPositions.
- Keep every test added by attempts 1 and 2 passing.

SCOPE
Encoding, parsing, doc comment, and tests only. No schema, no migration, no storage APIs, no context assembly, no CLI, no discovery edits. Do not change the comparator's field order or the projection logic.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
